subject: history
title: Causes of War Foundations
welcome_lead: Today you'll meet the key words historians use to explain why wars start.
meta_desc: GCSE History Causes of War foundations — MAIN causes, alliances and the road to conflict.
final_note: You learned the vocabulary historians use to analyse the causes of war.

concepts.def: Glorifying armed forces and building up weapons
A formal agreement to support another country
Building or controlling an empire abroad
Strong loyalty and pride in your own nation
Giving in to demands to avoid war
The short-term event that sets a war off

walkthroughs.body_html:
The MAIN causes of WWI: Militarism, Alliances, Imperialism, Nationalism.

Europe in 1914 was an arms race tied together by treaties — a small spark could pull everyone in.

On 28 June 1914, Archduke Franz Ferdinand was assassinated in Sarajevo by Gavrilo Princip.

Within six weeks the alliance system dragged Austria-Hungary, Germany, Russia, France and Britain into war.

The Treaty of Versailles left Germany angry. Hitler rearmed and took the Rhineland, Austria and the Sudetenland.

Britain's policy of appeasement hoped to avoid war. When Hitler invaded Poland on 1 September 1939, that hope ended.

mcqs.q: Which is NOT one of the MAIN causes of WWI?

options: Giving in to demands to avoid war

numericals.q: In which year was Archduke Franz Ferdinand assassinated?
numericals.hint: It happened the same year WWI began.

free_texts.q: What's the term for the short-term event that sets a war off? (one word, lowercase)
free_texts.hint: Like pulling the one on a gun — the immediate spark.
